title: I Thought I Had More Time
scene: You leave home earlier than usual to avoid rushing, but when you reach the station you discover a significant train delay. You briefly consider another route, then decide that waiting is still the better option.
sceneJa: 慌てないようにいつもより早く家を出たのに、駅で電車の大幅な遅延を知る場面。別ルートも考えるが、乗り換えの手間と比較して、その場で待つ方が得策だと判断する。

chunks.en: because I didn’t want to be in a rush.
chunks.ja: 慌てたくなかったので

chunks.en: When I got to the station,
that my train had been delayed
chunks.ja: 電車が遅れていることが

chunks.en: I considered taking a different route,
chunks.ja: 別ルートで行くことも考えました
でも、それだと必要になっていました

questions.question: Which chunking is most natural?
options: I decided / I was better off / waiting where I was
I decided I / was better / off waiting where / I was
I / decided I was / better off waiting / where I was
questions.explanation: ‘I decided’, ‘I was better off’, and ‘waiting where I was’ each form clear meaning groups.

questions.question: What does ‘would have involved changing trains twice’ mean?
options: The speaker had already changed trains twice
The alternative route would have required two train changes
The speaker needed to wait for two trains
questions.explanation: ‘Would have involved’ describes what the alternative option would have required.

questions.question: What does ‘I was better off waiting’ suggest?
options: Waiting was the more sensible option compared with the alternatives
The speaker was not allowed to leave
questions.explanation: ‘Be better off -ing’ means that doing something is the wiser or more advantageous choice.

speak: Read the opening with a relaxed, prepared tone. Pause slightly after ‘however’ to mark the unexpected delay. Let ‘For a moment’ sound thoughtful, then deliver ‘I was better off waiting where I was’ calmly, with ‘better off’ as one natural chunk.
review: Previous session: move beyond quick fixes by asking why a problem is happening in the first place. Useful chunks were ‘keep coming back’, ‘in the first place’, and ‘prevent it from happening again’. Today shifts to comparing options after an unexpected delay. Useful chunks are ‘be in a rush’, ‘would have involved ...’, and ‘be better off -ing’.
